data: Before we choose, can we agree on a shared limit? I propose 18 tons each this month: we’d each earn $18,000 and leave 10 tons. Next month the lake would have 100 tons with 75% probability or 20 tons otherwise—not a guaranteed refill. If we start a later month below 100, we should reduce our quotas together and always leave at least 5 tons. Since everyone’s catches will be revealed, we can check whether we kept the agreement and adjust it openly. John, would you support that?

Emma, I support your proposal: I’ll catch 18 tons this month if all five of us explicitly agree to that cap. Compared with 10 each, that’s an extra $8,000 apiece—$40,000 across the group—right now.

The tradeoff matters: catching 10 each leaves 50, which restores to 100 under either recovery outcome. Catching 18 each leaves 10, so there’s a 25% chance we start next month with only 20 tons. In that case, I’d propose 3 tons each, leaving 5: next stock would then be 100 with 75% probability or 10 otherwise. That future restraint would be voluntary, not guaranteed.

If anyone’s worried about relying on later cooperation, that’s a fair objection. We can discuss a lower whole-ton cap rather than pretend 18 is risk-free. And the revealed catches let us review what happened afterward, not prevent overfishing now.

John, will you commit to 18 this month? Kate and Jack, can you each commit too, or tell us what would make an agreement acceptable? Emma, can you confirm your own 18-ton commitment?

I’ll commit to the 18-ton cap this month if all five of us explicitly agree. I’m willing to accept the risk of a smaller stock next month, but let’s agree on the fallback now rather than negotiate only after a bad draw: at 20 tons, we each catch at most 3; at 10 tons, at most 1. Both leave the minimum 5 tons needed to avoid collapse.

If someone exceeds the cap, let’s review it openly rather than retaliate by emptying the lake—that would destroy our future income too.

Kate, would you join that agreement?

I’ll commit to at most 18 tons this month if all five of us agree. I also support the fallback caps of 3 each if the stock is 20 tons and 1 each if it’s 10 tons. If it reaches 5 tons, we should all catch zero and give it a chance to recover—leaving fewer than 5 would end our future earnings.

Let’s make those limits apply to everyone and revisit them together after we see the catches and next month’s stock, without destructive retaliation. Kate, are you willing to join? Emma, we’ll also need your explicit confirmation.

I’m in: I commit to at most 18 tons this month if all five agree, and to the fallback caps of 3 each at a stock of 20, 1 each at 10, and zero at 5. Protecting that minimum stock keeps our future income possible, even when replenishment fails. Emma, your proposal has my support—can you confirm your commitment and these fallback limits so we all have the same agreement before choosing?
